summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion is performed worldwide (~45–50 million/year). MTP Act (1971) legalized MTP in India with strict conditions to prevent illegal unsafe abortions. MTP Amendment Act: termination up to 12 weeks requires opinion of ONE Registered Medical Practitioner (RMP); termination from 12 to 24 weeks requires opinion of TWO RMPs. Medical regimen: Mifepristone (RU-486, progesterone receptor antagonist) followed by Misoprostol (PGE1 analog, induces uterine contractions).

MTP ACT LEGAL AMENDMENTS (INDIA)
                      
   MTP Act 1971 (Legalized to prevent maternal mortality from illegal unsafe abortions).
                                     │
   MTP Amendment Act (2017 / 2021):
   ├── Up to 12 Weeks Gestation (1st Trimester) ──► Requires opinion of ONE RMP.
   └── 12 to 24 Weeks Gestation (2nd Trimester) ──► Requires opinion of TWO RMPs.
conceptBreakdown.content:
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion is the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term.

### 7.1 Global & Indian Legal Landscape
- **Global Prevalence**: Approximately **$45\text{--}50\text{ million MTPs}$** are performed annually around the world (accounting for $\approx 1/5^{\text{th}}$ of total conceived pregnancies).
- **The MTP Act (1971 & Amendments)**:
  - Enacted by the Government of India in 1971 with strict conditions to prevent misuse and curb illegal, unsafe abortions.
  - **Permissible Grounds**: Failure of contraceptive device/method used by a couple, continuation of pregnancy involving risk to maternal life or physical/mental health, pregnancy resulting from rape, or substantial risk of serious physical/mental abnormalities in the fetus.
  - **Gestational Limits (Amendment Rules)**:
    - **First Trimester (Up to 12 Weeks)**: Safest window; requires the clinical opinion of **ONE Registered Medical Practitioner (RMP)**.
    - **Second Trimester (12 to 24 Weeks)**: Technically more complex; permitted for defined vulnerable categories (survivors of rape, minors, fetal anomalies) requiring the concurring opinion of **TWO Registered Medical Practitioners (RMPs)**.

### 7.2 Medical (Non-Surgical) Abortion Regimen: RU-486

```
                     MIFEPRISTONE (RU-486) ABORTION MECHANISM
                     
   Mifepristone (RU-486) ──► Potent Progesterone Receptor Antagonist
                                           │
   Endometrial Detachment ◄── Blocks Progesterone Action ──► Decidua Sloughs Off
                                           │
   Misoprostol (Prostaglandin E1) ─────────┴──► Induces Strong Uterine Contractions & Expulsion
```

1. **Mifepristone (RU-486)**: A synthetic steroid that acts as a competitive antagonist at progesterone receptors, blocking progesterone's sustaining effect on the endometrium, causing decidual ischemia, detachment, and hCG decline.
2. **Misoprostol**: A synthetic Prostaglandin $E_1$ (PGE$_1$) analog administered 24–48 hours later. It softens and dilates the cervix while stimulating rhythmic myometrial contractions to completely expel the detached conceptus.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Methotrexate-Misoprostol Regimen
conceptBreakdown.title: Methotrexate-Misoprostol Regimen
conceptBreakdown.content: Methotrexate (a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor) blocks rapidly dividing trophoblast cells and is used in medical management of early unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancies.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Second-Trimester MTP Risk Profile
conceptBreakdown.title: Second-Trimester MTP Risk Profile
conceptBreakdown.content: Abortion during the second trimester (weeks 13-24) carries significantly elevated maternal risks of uterine perforation, hemorrhage, sepsis, and amniotic fluid embolism compared to first-trimester MTP.
